newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ SHARP AGAIN AS EXPOS BEAT GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ SHARP AGAIN AS EXPOS BEAT GIANTS.

text.p: Pedro Martinez continued his torrid pitching by allowing just one run and two hits over seven innings and Doug Strange added a three-run homer as the Montreal Expos routed the San Francisco Giants 10-3 on Tuesday.

Martinez (5-0) became the league's third five-game winner, and saw his major-league leading ERA rise to just 0.50. He walked one and struck out 10 in going at least six innings for the fifth time in just five starts this season. In 36 1/3 innings thus far he has surrendered just two earned runs and 17 hits.
Martinez retired the first 12 batters of the game and the last eight he faced.
At Colorado, pitcher Bill Swift doubled home two runs in a four-run fourth inning and the Colorado Rockies erased an early four-run deficit and survived a 12-11 slugfest with the New York Mets.
Dante Bichette, Ellis Burks and Eric Young homered for Colorado, which collected 14 hits and scored 12 runs for the sixth time this season.
John Olerud had four hits, three RBI and three runs scored and Todd Hundley homered and drove in three runs for the Mets.
New York had 20 hits and stormed back from a five-run deficit of its own but left the bases loaded in the ninth.
"It's fun, a game like today," Mets manager Bobby Valentine said. "It would have been a lot more fun if we had won."

In Houston, Curt Schilling allowed one run over seven innings and Rico Brogna and Mike Lieberthal each drove in two runs as the Philadelphia Phillies used a four-run third inning to stop a three-game losing streak with a 5-1 victory over the Houston Astros.
Schilling (4-3), who was coming off consecutive losses, allowed seven hits, walked two and struck out seven as he improved to 5-4 overall versus Houston.
The Astros' Ramon Garcia gave up five runs and six hits with three walks and two strikeouts in two-plus innings.
In St Louis, former Brave Ron Gant's two-run homer with one out in the bottom of the eighth inning gave the St. Louis Cardinals a 4-3 victory over Atlanta and a split of the two-game series.

After the Braves took a 3-2 lead in the top of the eighth, Ray Lankford drew a one-out walk from reliever Mike Bielecki (1-2). Gant followed by crushing a 2-1 pitch over the left-centre field wall for his fourth homer and a 4-3 advantage.
"I know Bielecki," said Gant. "I've played with him. He knows me. I knew he was going to throw outside each time. When I connected I knew I had won the battle."

In San Diego, Kevin Foster surrendered just one run and six hits over seven innings, and Dave Hansen added a key two-run single in the seventh inning as the Chicago Cubs defeated the San Diego Padres, 2-1.
The Padres got their lone run in the third on a sacrifice fly by Quilvio Veras that scored Derrek Lee.
The Cubs had a chance to get on the board in the first when Brian McRae led off with a double and was sacrificed over. But Ashby struck out Grace and got Sosa on a groundout.
In Los Angeles, pinch-hitter Eduardo Perez homered with one out in the 11th inning to lift the Cincinnati Reds to a 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Mark Guthrie (1-1) retired Reggie Sanders on a flyout to start the 11th, but Perez batted for Reds closer Jeff Brantley (1-1) and hit a 2-2 pitch over the right-field fence for his first homer of the season.
"With the bases empty you look for a pitch and drive it," Perez said. "It was a fastball around letter high, definitely in my power area. I was just trying to throw some (bat) head out there."

At Florida, Steve Cooke and two relievers combined on a four-hitter and Tony Womack collected three hits as the Pittsburgh Pirates ended Florida's eight-game home winning streak with a 4-0 blanking of the Marlins.

Cooke (3-3) won his second straight start, allowing three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings. He improved to 4-0 lifetime against the Marlins. Ramon Morel pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings and Rich Loiselle worked the ninth.
"I ran into a little trouble in the first inning, the first inning always gives me trouble," Cooke said.
"I'm not going to baffle you on the radar gun. I've got a lot of heart and I battle," Cooke said.
